leaf.target: Cargo source replacement of crates.io with a local directory source
leaf.action: Inspected exactly the official Cargo Book Source Replacement page for crates.io-to-directory-source semantics and vendoring properties.

observed_scope: Source replacement redirects registry or git dependency communication to another source, including an exact local copy.
Vendoring can use a local-filesystem custom source which may be checked into a package.
The documented configuration defines a directory source and sets [source.crates-io] replace-with to that directory source.
A directory source contains unpacked crates on the local filesystem and is suitable for vendored dependencies.

leaf.result: At Cargo source-selection/configuration scope, a pre-populated local directory source can replace the crates.io source. Therefore the already-established version-only crates.io dependencies can, if their exact source packages are present in that directory and source replacement is configured, be resolved from local vendored content without runtime package-registry acquisition. The documentation also permits vendored sources to be checked into source control. This does not prove that a required vendor tree is already present, that initially populating it is zero-network/zero-user-execution, that all checksums/packages required by the lockfile are available, or that compilation/runtime behavior succeeds.

scope_guard: This checkpoint establishes only Cargo source-replacement semantics for replacing crates.io with a pre-populated local directory source and the resulting elimination of runtime package-registry acquisition at source-selection scope. It does not establish vendor-tree existence or provenance, initial population without network or user execution, complete lockfile coverage, actual Cargo offline execution, compilation, runtime proxy discovery, another version/project, or end-to-end richer-mode parity.
